audit_scope.description: This batch covers both EL and CL logic. EL scope includes EVM opcode execution (comparison ops, PUSH0, SELFDESTRUCT, CALL memory), JSON-RPC interface, block size validation, Ethash PoW verification, and Pectra EL fork activation. CL scope includes proposer lookahead computation (EIP-7917), Pectra CL fork activation, and the EIP inclusion governance process.

in_scope: EVM Opcode Execution (comparison, PUSH0, SELFDESTRUCT, CALL)
Validator deposit/exit mechanisms referenced by Pectra
out_of_scope: Execution Layer internals from CL perspective

misclassified_entities.reason: Internal EVM component. The calling contract is an in-scope internal entity executing within the EVM, not an external entity sending data into the system from outside the trust boundary.
Internal EVM component. The called contract executes within the same EVM sandbox and is not an external entity.
Governance-layer actor, not a runtime external entity. EIP proposers interact with the governance process, not with the running system at runtime.
Governance-layer actor, not a runtime external entity. Core developers review EIPs in a governance context, not at system runtime.
Governance-layer actor. Client teams implement EIPs offline, not as runtime external entities interacting with the system.

A light client is an internal node component requesting verification. While it could be modeled as external in some contexts, in the Ethash verification flow it is the local node itself performing light verification, not an external data source.

trusted_external_entities.name: User via JSON-RPC
trusted_external_entities.rationale: Public-facing RPC endpoint. No authentication required by default. Any external user or DApp can submit requests including malformed JSON, invalid parameters, or malicious transactions. Corresponds to EXT-RPC-CLIENT and EXT-TX-SUBMITTER from EIP-1474 subgraphs.

trusted_external_entities.name: Peer Node via P2P Network
trusted_external_entities.entry_point: P2P devp2p protocol (block propagation, transaction gossip)
trusted_external_entities.rationale: Unauthenticated P2P network peers. Any node can join and send blocks or transactions. Corresponds to EXT-PEER-NODE and EXT-MALICIOUS-PEER from EIP-7934, and EXT-BLOCK-PRODUCER from Ethash subgraphs. Peers may send oversized blocks, invalid PoW solutions, or malformed data.

trusted_external_entities.name: Transaction Sender via Signed Transaction
trusted_external_entities.entry_point: Transaction submission (via JSON-RPC or P2P gossip)
trusted_external_entities.rationale: Any externally owned account can craft and sign transactions. Transaction content (calldata, value, gas parameters) is fully attacker-controlled. Corresponds to EXT-TX-SENDER from EIP-6780 subgraph.

trusted_external_entities.name: Malicious Validator via Beacon P2P
trusted_external_entities.entry_point: Beacon chain P2P gossip (block proposals, attestations)
trusted_external_entities.rationale: Validators are staked but not trusted. A validator may attempt to manipulate proposer selection via effective balance grinding (EIP-7917), propose invalid blocks, or submit conflicting attestations. Corresponds to EXT-MALICIOUS-VALIDATOR from EIP-7917 subgraph.

trusted_external_entities.name: Beacon Network (RANDAO reveals)
trusted_external_entities.rationale: RANDAO values are revealed through block proposals on the P2P network. While the protocol enforces RANDAO correctness via slashing, the network itself is unauthenticated. Corresponds to EXT-NETWORK from EIP-7917 subgraph.

trusted_external_entities.name: Consensus Layer via Engine API
trusted_external_entities.rationale: Authenticated via JWT between co-located EL and CL clients. The CL is a trusted local component, but payload content (blocks from the network) must still be validated by the EL. This is an archetypal attack vector: the CL forwards untrusted network data over a trusted channel.

trusted_external_entities.name: MEV-Boost Relay via External API
trusted_external_entities.entry_point: MEV-Boost relay API (block bids, execution payloads)
trusted_external_entities.rationale: Archetypal CL attack vector. External MEV relays provide block bids and execution payloads. They are third-party services with no on-chain accountability. May provide censored, invalid, or manipulated payloads.

boundary_edges.security_assumption: Full input validation required: JSON parsing, RPC structure validation, method lookup, parameter validation, hex encoding checks. Rate limiting recommended to prevent DoS.

Full transaction validation required: hex decoding, RLP parsing, ECDSA signature verification, nonce checks, balance checks, gas limit validation. Malformed or invalid transactions must be rejected before entering the mempool.

Block size validation (EIP-7934: <= 8 MiB RLP-encoded) must occur early before expensive processing. Full block validation including PoW/PoS checks, state transition, and header verification required.
Full PoW verification required: seed hash computation, 64-iteration mix loop, difficulty check. Invalid PoW must be rejected. (Legacy pre-merge; still relevant for historical sync.)
Same-transaction creation check must be correct to enforce EIP-6780 restrictions. Incorrect tracking could allow unauthorized state deletion or prevent legitimate destruction.

Effective balance values must be locked at lookahead distance before RANDAO reveal. Validators cannot manipulate EB after seeing RANDAO to influence proposer selection. The MIN_SEED_LOOKAHEAD separation must be enforced.
RANDAO values from MIN_SEED_LOOKAHEAD + 1 epochs prior must be unpredictable at EB-setting time. Protocol must enforce correct RANDAO reveals via slashing.

JWT authentication validates the channel, but payload content (blocks forwarded from CL) must be fully validated by the EL: state transition, gas accounting, block size limits, all EIP rules. The CL forwards untrusted network data.

All block bids and execution payloads from relays must be fully validated. Relay responses are not authenticated on-chain. The CL must verify payload validity before proposing. Censorship and invalid payload attacks are possible.
